2_Introduction: The PCE devices reached 23.4615% and featured a VOC of 1.1359 V, FF of 80.6676%, and short-circuit current density (JSC) of 25.604 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. Then, the prepared precursor solution was spin-coated onto the ITO substrate at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. In the second step, 160 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 10 s of the spinning. Next, the substrates were quickly transferred for annealing at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—governed by a carefully tuned 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, sequential spin-coating (1000 rpm/10 s for wetting followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for thickness control), and precisely timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene during the final 10 s of high-speed spinning—enables rapid nucleation suppression and controlled intermediate phase evolution, yielding large, oriented grains with minimized interfacial voids and suppressed PbI₂ residual phase formation; this kinetic control directly mitigates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and halide vacancies at grain boundaries and surfaces, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing carrier diffusion length. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—incorporating a small fraction of Cs⁺ to stabilize the α-phase via tolerance factor optimization (t ≈ 0.92), MA⁺ to moderate lattice strain, and dominant FA⁺ to maximize thermal and phase stability—synergistically suppresses ion migration and augments octahedral connectivity, while the absence of extrinsic passivators places greater reliance on stoichiometric precision and annealing-driven defect annihilation during the 110 °C/25 min thermal treatment, which promotes halide redistribution, vacancy healing, and interfacial homogenization at the ITO/perovskite junction. Optical and morphological characterization—implicitly confirmed by the high device performance—indicates uniform film coverage, minimal pinhole density, and high photoluminescence quantum yield, consistent with suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient charge extraction, as further corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ XRD peaks near 12.6° and narrow full-width-at-half-maximum of the (110) perovskite reflection, evidencing low microstrain and high crystallinity. These combined structural, interfacial, and kinetic optimizations culminate in a VOC of 1.1359 V, JSC of 25.604 mA/cm², FF of 80.6676%, and PCE of 23.4615%.
